countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.

universities.summary: Vellore Institute of Technology is a private deemed-to-be university founded in 1984 and granted university status in 2001. Its main campus is in Vellore, with an approved off-campus centre in Chennai. Regular degrees include engineering, sciences, commerce, hospitality and business. Entry and fees depend on the programme, teaching campus and Indian, NRI or foreign applicant route.
universities.campusLifestyle: The Vellore campus is VIT's original site and the largest of its four campuses. Its NIRF 2025 engineering submission records 35,957 students on four-year undergraduate programmes, 2,600 on two-year postgraduate programmes and 6,308 on five-year integrated programmes, including 1,408 students from outside India. Facilities include the Periyar E.V.R. Central Library, an air-conditioned gymnasium, indoor and outdoor sports grounds, a swimming pool, campus-wide Wi-Fi, general stores and a pharmacy. Teaching runs on VIT's Fully Flexible Credit System, which lets students choose electives, faculty and slots rather than following a fixed timetable.
universities.cityProfile: VIT’s main campus is at Katpadi, Vellore 632014, in northern Tamil Nadu. Its separate approved Chennai off-campus centre has its own teaching and accommodation arrangements. Confirm the campus stated on the offer before making travel or housing payments. VIT-AP and VIT Bhopal are separate universities and their programmes and charges are not interchangeable with Vellore or Chennai.
universities.practicalExposure: Practical exposure at Vellore is built around industry-partnered degrees, credit mobility and campus recruitment. Named industry-linked programmes include B.Tech. Computer Science and Engineering and Business Systems delivered with TCS, B.Tech. Civil Engineering in collaboration with L&T, M.Tech. Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning with LTIMindtree as knowledge partner, and B.Com. specialisations run with NSE Academy and TCS. VIT's International Transfer Programme offers 2+2 bachelor's, 1+1 master's, 3+2 and 3.5+1.5 accelerated pathways with partner universities abroad, and is available in seven engineering disciplines: Computer Science and Engineering, Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Electronics and Communication Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Civil Engineering and Biotechnology. VIT states it holds more than 500 memoranda of understanding with foreign universities and is a partner in the European Commission-funded Erasmus+ CBHE HARMONY project on internationalisation, led by the University of Zaragoza. On placement outcomes, VIT's NIRF 2025 submission for the Vellore campus records 4,031 of 5,964 graduating four-year undergraduates placed in 2023-24 at a median salary of INR 899,000, and 884 of 1,270 two-year postgraduates placed at a median of INR 915,000.
universities.hostelOverview: The Vellore campus has 32 hostel blocks - 21 for men and the remainder for women - housing over 30,000 residents a year. NRI and foreign students pay in USD on a separate published tariff. For 2026-27 the men's regular blocks range from USD 2,170 for a six-bed non-air-conditioned room with vegetarian mess to USD 3,240 for a two-bed air-conditioned room with special mess, and the women's blocks from USD 2,680 for a four-bed air-conditioned bunker-cot room to USD 3,950 for a three-bed apartment room. Each figure covers room, mess, a non-refundable USD 250 admission fee and a refundable USD 400 caution deposit, and includes laundry up to 44 washes. Rooms are allotted first come, first served and the hostel fee is paid separately from tuition.
universities.dietarySupport: Hostel fees are quoted as room-plus-mess packages, so meals are prepaid rather than pay-as-you-go. Students choose between vegetarian, non-vegetarian and special mess tiers at the Vellore campus, and VIT states its catering serves vegetarian, non-vegetarian and international palates. Mess selection can be changed monthly, but upgrading in the fall semester requires paying the full differential and there is no refund for downgrading a mess or room.
universities.safetyOverview: Hostel premises have round-the-clock security personnel, and each block is staffed by supervisors, student counsellors and maintenance staff. A hostel review committee meets once a fortnight to take resident queries. VIT runs a primary health centre in the Dr. A.L. Mudaliar Block on campus with a pharmacy, two consultation rooms, an emergency room and 24-hour doctor and nursing cover.
universities.studentSupport: The International Relations Office in Dr. M.G.R. Block handles NRI and foreign admissions and every international student registers there on the day of admission. It is reachable at global@vit.ac.in and by phone on +91-416-220-2070 or +91-416-220-2072. VIT also operates an Equal Opportunity Cell, a Student Grievance Redressal Committee, an Internal Complaints Committee, a disability support service and the Centre for VIT Happiness and Well Being.
whyChoose: Foreign nationals and NRI applicants can be admitted to B.Tech. directly on Class 12 or equivalent results, with no requirement to sit VITEEE - a genuinely separate channel from the domestic entrance-test route.

Two US accreditors recognise VIT's Vellore provision: VIT states that its B.Tech. Computer Science and Engineering is accredited by both the Computing Accreditation Commission and the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, and its B.Tech. Electronics and Communication Engineering by the ABET Engineering Accreditation Commission, while VIT Business School, which teaches the Vellore MBA, appears as an accredited school in the AACSB business school directory.

Tuition for every international programme is published in USD on VIT's own international fee page for 2026-27, including USD 9,000 a year for B.Tech. and USD 6,450 a year for the MBA, so the cost is knowable before applying.

NAAC accredited VIT at A++ grade with a CGPA of 3.66 in its fourth assessment cycle, declared in August 2021, and NIRF 2025 placed VIT at 14th among universities, 16th in engineering and 21st overall in India.

Four B.Tech programmes at the Vellore campus hold National Board of Accreditation Tier I accreditation under the Washington Accord, running to 30 June 2031 - Chemical, Electrical and Electronics, Electronics and Instrumentation, and Mechanical Engineering.
The International Transfer Programme allows part of a VIT degree to be completed at a partner university abroad through 2+2, 1+1, 3+2 and 3.5+1.5 structures across seven engineering disciplines.
thingsToConsider: An Indian Student visa prohibits employment or business activity, so there is no part-time work income to offset costs; students must also open an NRO bank account and give the details to the FRRO.

VIT allots the B.Tech. branch after reviewing the application and supporting documents, and states that the branch once allotted will not be changed under any circumstances - so applicants cannot count on switching specialisation after arrival.

Foreign applicants who studied Physics, Chemistry and Biology without Mathematics are restricted to a short named list of bio-related B.Tech. programmes, and at the Vellore campus that means Biotechnology, Computer Science and Engineering (Bioinformatics) or Health Sciences and Technology, with a compulsory bridge course in Mathematics after joining.

Applicants from boards outside VIT's recognised-equivalence list must obtain a University Grants Commission equivalence certificate, which is mandatory at the time of admission rather than at application.

The NRI category requires sponsorship by a parent living abroad plus that parent's employer certificate; sponsorship by a relative or friend is not accepted, so the NRI route is not a general discount channel.

VIT marks its published international application deadlines as tentative and states that hostel fees are subject to annual escalation, so the 31 August 2026 B.Tech. and 30 June 2026 other-programme dates should be treated as provisional.

faq.question: Which VIT locations are included?
faq.answer: Vellore is the main campus and Chennai is an approved off-campus centre of the same deemed university. Each programme title names its location. VIT-AP and VIT Bhopal are separate universities; their degree lists, entrance conditions, campus facilities and prices should be checked separately.

faq.question: What is the difference between a two-year and an integrated MSc?
faq.answer: The two-year MSc requires a qualifying undergraduate degree in the named subject group. The five-year integrated MSc begins after Higher Secondary with programme-specific science subjects. Bachelor or honours exits within an integrated route are subject to its rules and are not interchangeable with a separate three-year admission.

faq.question: Which routes use VITMEE?
faq.answer: The current Indian MSc Data Science and Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning routes use VITMEE, campus preferences, merit and available seats. The listed non-entrance academic MSc programmes select on qualifying undergraduate marks. Existing international entry routes have their own conditions.

faq.question: Can NRI and foreign applicants use the academic UG listings?
faq.answer: Yes, the named academic UG routes have a separate international application. NRI applicants need sponsorship by a parent working abroad; the foreign category lists foreign passport/ID holders and OCI. Exact subjects, marks and documents differ by degree and category. These conditions do not establish the domestic route.

faq.question: What marks do academic UG international applicants need?
faq.answer: For the listed Computer Science, Commerce and media degrees, the current route generally requires 60% overall for NRI applicants and 55% or grade equivalent for foreign applicants, plus the named subject requirements. Hospitality accepts a pass in any qualifying stream or a recognised 10+3 diploma. NRI age and sponsorship conditions also apply.

faq.question: How is Agriculture admission different?
faq.answer: The resident Indian route requires 60% overall and 60% in Physics, Chemistry and Biology, with the published category concessions. There is no entrance examination; the university prepares a qualifying-examination merit rank and conducts counselling. Agriculture has three tuition categories, so the lowest rate is not a guaranteed allotment.

faq.question: What should I budget beyond the displayed fees?
faq.answer: Ask for the complete written campus and category-specific amount, including caution deposits, compulsory academic charges, laboratory or project costs, hostel and mess. Annual programme-fee quotes are not automatically isolated tuition. Integrated Biotechnology has a separate higher fourth- and fifth-year rate.

faq.question: Are there subject-specific conditions for the MSc?
faq.answer: Yes. Business Statistics requires Mathematics at both 10+2 and degree level. Physics requires a three-year BSc with Physics major; Chemistry requires the stated chemistry/applied-science degree and ancillary subjects. Biological master’s accept their listed biological-science or biotechnology qualifications. Read the exact subject list before applying.

faq.question: Does Biomedical Genetics qualify me for clinical practice?
faq.answer: The MSc is an academic degree and Genetic Counselling is an optional specialisation. An admission listing does not itself establish registration or a licence to practise a regulated clinical profession. Confirm any separate credential required for the role and jurisdiction you intend to enter.

faq.question: When is the next intake?
faq.answer: Obtain the current programme and campus admission announcement directly. The captured 2026 deadlines have passed and are not a promise that applications remain open. A start month is shown only where the individual published route has supported evidence; no date is carried across campuses.

faq.question: What teaching language should I expect?
faq.answer: Language information is retained where established for a programme. Where the current named route does not establish the teaching language, obtain written confirmation from the department before accepting. English as a school subject or an entrance-test language does not alone define all teaching and examinations.

faq.question: How should I confirm my eligibility?
faq.answer: Select the exact award and campus, then use its Indian, NRI or foreign application route. Check the qualifying institution, degree or board, subjects, marks, mode of study and any equivalence/category documents. Confirm the complete offer and payment terms before arranging accommodation or travel.

evidence.claimText: The University Grants Commission is the statutory body of the Government of India for coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education, operating under the Ministry of Education.
evidence.internalNotes: UGC publishes the authoritative lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, plus a published list of fake universities. Corroborated by the Study in India portal Indian Higher Education page, which states all institutions are governed by the Ministry of Education.

evidence.claimText: The All India Council for Technical Education is the Government of India statutory body for technical education, covering engineering, management and allied technical programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) - official site

evidence.claimText: The National Medical Commission is the Government of India regulator for medical education and medical institutions; medical and dental admission is governed separately from general higher education.
India's higher-education landscape includes over 1,100 universities and more than 45,000 colleges, all governed by the Ministry of Education, and higher education begins after 12 years of schooling.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Indian Higher Education
evidence.internalNotes: Portal-published counts are approximate and shift between AISHE cycles; treat them as indicative and re-check at review. Regulator identity is separately verified against UGC and AICTE.

evidence.claimText: The Study in India portal is the Government of India route for international applicants: the applicant registers for a compulsory SII ID, explores participating institutes and courses, submits applications to several institutes from one profile, accepts an offer letter, then applies for a student visa or student e-visa.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - official portal

evidence.claimText: The Bureau of Immigration directs foreign nationals who wish to apply to Indian institutes to register under the Study in India scheme, confirming the portal as a government-recognised route rather than a third-party service.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations administers Government of India scholarship schemes for international students at UG, PG and PhD level, including AYUSH streams; applications are handled through the ICCR A2A scholarship portal and the applicant's Indian diplomatic mission.
evidence.sourceLabel: ICCR Admissions to Alumni (A2A) Scholarship Portal
evidence.internalNotes: Portal states that applicants should contact the Indian Mission for scholarship updates - eligibility and open cycles are mission-specific and vary by country, so no scheme may be presented as open to all nationalities.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. Student (S-3) visas cover yoga, Vedic culture, Indian dance, music and Buddhist studies at approved institutions; Student (S-5) visas cover internships.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival. Pakistani nationals must register within 24 hours. Children under 12 years and OCI cardholders are exempt from registration, and citizens of Nepal and Bhutan are exempt from both visa and registration requirements.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Registration Requirements
evidence.internalNotes: Corroborated by the Study in India Onboarding & FRRO page, which states e-FRRO registration within 14 days of landing. Nationality-dependent rule - never state one universal deadline.

evidence.claimText: Students on an Indian Student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, must open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account with a recognised Indian bank and furnish the details to the FRRO, and must not enrol in off-campus franchise centres, distance-learning study centres of open universities or outreach programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India
evidence.internalNotes: Directly constrains any work-rights or earn-while-you-study claim on India pages. Do not publish part-time work guidance for India.

evidence.claimText: An applicant should possess proof of admission to a full-time regular academic course at a recognised Indian institution and evidence of financial support, and must also hold a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Health where the admission is to a medical or paramedical course.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Onboarding & FRRO
evidence.internalNotes: The portal adds its own disclaimer that document requirements differ across countries and must be confirmed with the nearest Indian embassy.

evidence.claimText: The National Assessment and Accreditation Council, established in 1994 as an autonomous institution of the UGC, assesses and accredits Indian higher education institutions. The National Institutional Ranking Framework, launched by the Ministry of Education in September 2015, is the government ranking framework for Indian institutions.
evidence.internalNotes: NIRF corroborated separately at https://www.nirfindia.org/Home (MoE, launched 29 September 2015). Use a NAAC grade or NIRF rank only with the assessment or ranking year stated.

evidence.claimText: India spans Himalayan, tropical coastal, semi-arid and monsoon-affected climate zones, with the southwest monsoon typically running from June to September.
evidence.sourceLabel: India Meteorological Department, Ministry of Earth Sciences
evidence.internalNotes: General climatic framing only; do not present city-level weather claims at country level.

evidence.claimText: NAAC accredited Vellore Institute of Technology at A++ grade with a CGPA of 3.66 on a four-point scale in Cycle 4, declared on 31 August 2021.

evidence.internalNotes: Verified against the regulator's own workbook by research/india-regulator-verification-2026-08-22.md (agent claude-india-regverify-20260822, checked 2026-08-22); workbook row AISHE U-0490, Katpadi-Thiruvalam Road, Vellore.
